analysis.file_name: GS Blekos - ## Global Macro Goal Kickstart Apple Allianz DSV Gjensidige M&A Basket Unibail Building Mats Solaria Argenx ## 27 Oct 2026.pdf
analysis.title: Global Macro / Goal Kickstart / Apple / Allianz / DSV / Gjensidige / M&A Basket / Unibail / Building Mats / Solaria / Argenx
key_insights: Global growth has been unremarkable in 2026, with fiscal easing and the AI boom offsetting drags from energy and tariffs. GS baseline for 2027 is a similar pace, but downside risks are building from higher energy prices, higher bond yields and possibly slower AI investment growth.
GS expects fewer rate hikes than priced for most major DM central banks, because AI labor market effects are becoming more visible and inflation is likely to decline.
GS Goal Kickstart: the Risk Appetite Indicator is negative as Tech dominates cross-asset moves.
GS asset allocation stays modestly pro-risk: overweight Equities for 3m/12m, underweight Credit for 3m/12m, overweight Cash for 3m and overweight Bonds for 12m.
AI concerns, Middle East tensions and mid-term elections could sustain near-term volatility, but GS expects earnings support, lighter positioning and lower valuations to help equities into year-end.

Apple F4Q26 preview: GS expects in-line results, with iPhone revenue +15% y/y on price increases on the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max and older models plus the Duo launch, offsetting modest volume declines and the delayed iPhone 18 launch.

Apple F4Q26 preview: GS expects Services revenue +10% y/y despite slowing App Store growth, with iCloud+, AppleCare+, subscriptions and advertising growing double-digits. Gross margin is expected at 47.8%, including a 1pp benefit from tariff refunds and headwinds from component cost inflation.
Allianz reports 3Q'26 on November 12. GS operating profit estimate is c.1% below company-collected consensus (published 26/10/26), driven by P&C (-2%) and Asset Management (-2%).
Allianz P&C estimate is lower on a headline combined ratio c.15bps less favourable and c.2% lower Insurance Revenue. GS expects focus on rate and volume trends in Commercial and Retail lines.
DSV: GS reiterates Buy (on Conviction List) with a 12m DCF-based price target unchanged at DKK 2,300. 2026-30 estimates move little, EPS down slightly and FCF up slightly (+/-2% on average).

DSV earnings power has risen since the DBS deal. Quarterly EBIT was ~DKK 4bn when the deal was announced in 2024 and DKK 6.3bn in Q326, with Road running c. DKK 1bn per quarter behind schedule. GS expects DKK 7-8bn quarterly EBIT during 2027.

Gjensidige downgraded to Neutral as GS expects pricing to normalise with claims inflation moderating, leaving limited room to beat high expectations. Earn-through of prior pricing should still support profitability, but margin expansion becomes more measured.
GS cuts Gjensidige FY27e-30e EPS by c.2.4% on average on lower growth and margin expansion.

GS rebalanced its European M&A basket (GSTRACQN) with additions Abivax, Haleon, Moncler, Burberry, Prada, Swatch Group, Rightmove, Scout24 and Zegona. About 65% of the basket is Industrials, Consumer Discretionary and Healthcare, and c.35% is UK-domiciled.

Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield: GS maintains Buy after 9M26 results. 2026E-2030E EPS is down 0-2% on higher refinancing costs, and management reiterated 2028 guidance but closer to the lower end. 12m PT cut 2% to €121.0 from €124.0, implying 34% upside.

The briefing also lists, by headline only, a note on US residential roofing supply/demand challenges (Europe Building Materials), Solaria (a 'fundamental dislocation') and an Argenx management roadshow on Vyvgart growth.
